learning_outcomes.text: Assimilation by students of the basic laws and concepts in the field of thermodynamics.
Practical use of theoretical knowledge when solving problems in the field of mathematical tasks and exercises.
Preparing students to conduct scientific research.

syllabus_topics: Subject and methods of thermodynamic research. Basic concepts and definitions. Substance and energy.
Types of energy. Work and heat as ways of transferring energy between thermodynamic systems. The first law of thermodynamics.
Energy balance of closed and open systems. Substance models.
An ideal gas as an example of a simple system. Properties, equations and characteristic transformations of ideal gases.
Polytropic changes. Entropy and reversibility. Irreversibility and dissipation effects. Thermodynamic cycles and model gas cycles of thermal devices.
Internal combustion engines, refrigerators and heating pumps. Thermal efficiency of motor circuits and coefficient of performance of cooling and heating circuits.
The Second Law of Thermodynamics and its equivalent formulations. Characteristic irreversible changes. Fundamentals of thermostatic gas mixtures.
Parameters and transformations of humid air. Saturated and superheated steam: properties and characteristic transformations. Real gases.
Systems of units. International System of Units SI.
Using the equation of state and other mathematical relationships to determine the parameters of the ideal gas state and its specific heat.
Balancing the energy exchange between the thermodynamic system and the environment on the basis of the first law of thermodynamics.
Quantitative analysis of energy conversion processes - determination of energy quantities (heat, volumetric work and technical work) characterizing reversible transformations of ideal gases.
Interpretation of polytropic transformations on diagrams of work and heat.
Qualitative analysis of energy conversion processes - determination of energy conversion efficiency on the basis of the second law of thermodynamics.
Determination of the thermal efficiency of engine gas cycles and coefficient of performance of gas cooling and heating cycles.
Calculation of parameters of humid air and analysis of its typical thermodynamic transformations.
Determining the properties of saturated and superheated steam using tables and graphs.
Interpretation of characteristic transformations of saturated and superheated steam on diagrams; work, heat and the Mollier diagram.
Measurement of the heat of combustion.
Measurement of the moisture content of solid fuels.
Determination of the characteristics of the resistance temperature sensor
Determination of air humidity.
Marking of pressure gauges for measuring high pressures.
Marking micromanometers.
Measurements of calorific value of solid and liquid fuels.
Thermocouple gauge.
Measurement of the relative viscosity of liquids.
Isothermal transformation.
Isobaric transformation.
Isochoric transformation.
Determination of the ignition temperature of liquid fuels using the Pensky-Martens method.
Determination of superheated steam parameters
teaching_methods: Conventional lecture with the use of audiovisual means
assessment_rules: The condition for passing a subject is to obtain all the required learning outcomes specified for a given subject. Obtaining positive grades in all forms of classes included in a given subject is tantamount to passing it and obtaining by the student the number of ECTS points assigned to this subject. The method of calculating the final grade for the course is specified in the study regulations.
